errors.evidence: The y-axis has values that exceed 0.8 (e.g., the pink bars for the last two models are greater than 0.8). The visible gridlines go up to 0.8, but the axis itself extends further, likely to 1.0.

errors.text_span: The “Single-task_baseline” model shows the lowest performance across all tasks
errors.evidence: This claim is incorrect. While the 'Single-task_baseline' model has the lowest STS Corr. score (~0.5), it has the highest Sentiment Acc. (~0.54) and Paraphrase Acc. (~0.79) scores among all models.

errors.text_span: shows a significant improvement in STS Corr.
errors.evidence: The description makes a subjective claim about a "significant improvement." It should stick to describing the data points objectively.

errors.text_span: The “Supervised_SimCSE” model achieves the highest scores across all tasks
errors.evidence: This claim is false. For this model, the Sentiment Acc. score is one of the lowest, and its Paraphrase Acc. score is lower than that of the 'Single-task_baseline' model. Its STS Corr. score is also slightly lower than the '2-Tier SimCSE' model's score.

errors.text_span: The “2-Tier SimCSE” model achieves the highest scores across all tasks
errors.evidence: This claim is false. While this model has the highest STS Corr. score, its Sentiment Acc. score is one of the lowest, and its Paraphrase Acc. score is lower than that of the 'Single-task_baseline' model. This also contradicts the previous sentence.
The STS Corr. value for 'Supervised_SimCSE' is visibly higher than the 0.8 gridline, approximately 0.81.
The STS Corr. value for '2-Tier SimCSE' is visibly higher than the value for 'Supervised_SimCSE' and is approximately 0.82, not 0.81.
